query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys reported to date commonly contain both solid solutions and intermetallic compounds. Induction-melted Al- and Mg-rich alloys reached densities of 2.64–2.75 g/cm3 but all had complex structures; Al20Be20Fe10Si15Ti35 combined a density of 3.91 g/cm3 with 911 HV hardness and oxidation resistance at 700 and 900 °C; compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd showed region-dependent compression, plasticity, and corrosion behavior; and reported AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys contained a primary BCC constituent together with intermetallic compounds, with x = 1.0 showing the best property combination in that series. Prior studies have emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, whereas interfacial segregation, interfacial energy, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance remain insufficiently studied. The design must retain a density below 6 g/cm3 and address performance constraints associated with the tendency of Mg and dissimilar constituent elements to form stable intermetallic compounds. Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state, what single intervention hypothesis could improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance? State the intervention, its proposed causal mechanism, quantitative or directional predictions relative to the as-processed baseline, the composition and operating or test boundaries, the prior experimental evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with explicit observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Mo to a Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy will improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance by forming a stable σ phase and enhancing the formation of a protective MoO3 layer.
generation.conditions: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a density below 6 g/cm3
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of σ phase and MoO3 layer
generation.mechanism: Slip frustration hardening (SFH) of nano NiAl precipitates and precipitation hardening of σ phase, as well as the formation of a stable MoO3 protective layer
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation), enhanced corrosion resistance, and improved high-temperature oxidation resistance
generation.baseline: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy without Mo addition
generation.boundary: Density below 6 g/cm3, Mg and dissimilar constituent elements forming stable intermetallic compounds
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Mo addition required to achieve optimal performance, and the potential effects of Mo addition on other properties such as ductility and fracture toughness

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys with varying amounts of Mo addition, and test their mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Mo does not result in improved mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation properties, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text:
Effect of Mo on the Mechanical and Corrosion Behaviors in Non-Equal Molar AlCrFeMnNi BCC High-Entropy Alloys

Abstract: AbstractCo-free body-centered cubic (bcc) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are prepared, and the elevated mechanical property and corrosion property of the Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5Mox (x = 0 and 0.1) alloys are studied. The Vickers hardness (HV) of the as-homogenized state is between HV 350 and HV 400. Both alloys are provided with nano-scale NiAl-rich B2 precipitates which contribute to the strength at high-temperature. In addition, adding Mo in the present alloy strengthens by σ phase. Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5Mo0.1 exhibited outstanding tensile properties, with a yield strength of 413 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of 430 MPa in the elevated tensile test at 600 °C, which is better than that of Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5 alloy. Through potentiodynamic polarization testing in 0.5 M H2SO4 solution and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), it is shown that adding Mo can effectively reduce the corrosion current density and improve the impedance of passive film, since the passivation layer is formed and stable.Keywords: high-entropy alloys, body centered cubic, NiAl precipitates,
